title: micro-skill-stash-hire-sprint-and-async-eval-rubric
body:
Purpose:
Create a lightweight, repeatable 14-day hiring sprint that seeds a small internal bench ("micro-skill stash") of screened, cross-trained contributors for product and infra teams. Goal is to shorten time-to-fill for high-velocity roles (SWE IC, SRE IC, Solutions Eng) and reduce time-to-productivity by standardizing an asynchronous evaluation rubric + a targeted 14-day onboarding capsule.

Scope and when to use this playbook:
- Use for roles with predictable task patterns and a steady hiring cadence (contract-to-perm, surge headcount, trial roles).
- Not intended for senior leadership, deeply research-heavy hires, or fully bespoke roles.
- Designed to be lean: ~6–12 candidates per sprint, 2 hiring owners (PM/Eng partner + People Ops), and a small evaluation panel that uses async scoring.

Sprint timeline (14 days):
Day 0: Open intake, post requisition, enable referrals and internal float-list.
Day 1–4: Resume triage + asynchronous work sample distributed (2 small tasks; total ~90–120 minutes).
Day 5–7: Panel scoring window (asynchronous rubric, comments required). Candidate follow-ups scheduled only for edge cases.
Day 8–10: Interview-lite for top 40% (45 minute focused sync if needed). Offer calibration.
Day 11–14: Offer + prep for 14-day onboarding capsule start.

Responsibilities (owners):
- Hiring partner (eng/product): craft 2 short work samples and the role-locked checklist; commit a reviewer-hour budget.
- People Ops: sprint orchestration, posting, candidate comms cadence, offer template, onboarding capsule packaging.
- Panel reviewers: evaluate asynchronously within scoring window, leave 3 concise notes linked to rubric anchors.

Asynchronous evaluation rubric (flat 1–5 scale; required fields):
Scoring anchors (1=Fail, 3=Meets bar, 5=Outstanding). Provide numeric score and 1–2 sentence evidence.
- Problem Decomposition (technical roles): clarity of approach, tradeoffs, edgecases considered.
- Practical Implementation (work sample): code readability, maintainability, small decisions (testing, error handling).
- Systems Judgment (infra/SRE): risk assessment, operational controls, failure modes.
- Documentation & Handoff (all roles): ability to clearly explain work product for a peer to pick up.
- Collaboration Signals (soft skills): concise async communication, response timeliness, constructive feedback in sample exchange.

Rubric example row (for reviewers to paste into comment):
> Problem Decomposition: 4 — Proposed clean decomposition; missed one edge case (long tail input).
> Implementation: 3 — Solution works, some duplication, would add 1 unit test.
> Systems Judgment: N/A — not applicable for this task.
> Docs & Handoff: 4 — README sufficient to reproduce locally.
> Collaboration: 5 — polite, fast replies and incorporated reviewer note.

Decision rules (fast, transparent):
- Auto-accept: candidate with average >= 4.2 across applicable anchors and no score of 1.
- Hold/Follow: avg between 3.4–4.19 or any single 1–2 with strong written mitigation from candidate.
- Reject: avg < 3.4 or explicit fail on a core axis.

Calibration guidance for reviewers: leave concrete evidence, avoid vague phrases ("looks good"). If you give a 1–2, explain gate failure (security risk, inability to complete required part). Each reviewer must add at least one improvement suggestion per candidate.

Candidate comms templates (short):
- Invite to work sample: "Thanks for applying — we have a 2-task work sample (~90m). Please complete in the next 72 hours. Submit via our portal or GitHub Gist"
- After async review (positive): "We liked your submission and want to invite you to a short sync to cover one follow-up area."
- Decline: single-line personalized decline + optional feedback bucket (3 bullets).

14-day onboarding capsule (first two weeks; aim: rapid contribution):
Pre-start (offer accepted -> Day 0): access checklist (email, SSO, VPN, laptop image request), 1 pager role context, first-week microgoals.
Day 1: orientation (30m people-ops), team sync (30m), access verification, dev environment setup task (small repo clone + run tests).
Day 2–3: buddy pairing (shadow small task), delivery of first microtask (<=4 hours) scoped by hiring partner.
Day 4–7: growth tasks (owner-driven) + daily 15m async stand via Slack thread. Weekly demo: short PR or doc showing progress.
Day 8–12: cross-training on adjacent area (monitoring runbook, infra sanity check, or product feature toggle flow).
Day 13–14: retro + success signal check (owner, buddy, people-ops) and transition plan to normal cadence.

First-week microtasks (examples):
- Clone the infra repo, run the e2e smoke script, and file one improvement issue.
- Add a small unit test to an existing module and open PR.
- Write a 1-paragraph README for a small internal tool used by the team.

Success metrics for the micro-skill stash pilot (first 3 months):
- Time-to-offer: median <= 10 days from job post.
- Time-to-first-meaningful-PR: median <= 12 days from start.
- Offer accept rate: >= 70% for bench-sourced candidates.
- Reviewer throughput: panel average review time <= 48 hours.

Risk controls and mitigations:
- Quality slip: escalate candidate with borderline scores to a live sync before offer.
- Volume oversubscribe: cap intake per sprint; keep rolling float-list for next sprint.
- Data privacy: work sample artifacts stored in secured bucket and access-logged.

Operational notes (playback & tooling):
- Use a single shared spreadsheet (Hiring sprint tracker) with candidate stage, avg score, reviewer notes, offer status, and onboarding capsule assignment.
- Create a dedicated Slack thread per sprint for questions and asynchronous calibration notes.
- People Ops to run weekly 30m retro with hiring partners for the first 4 sprints.

Open questions to iterate on after pilot:
- Should we codify the microtask library by role to speed up sample generation?
- Which roles are poor fits for async-only evaluation? (capture evidence during pilot)
- Budget model: when to convert bench hires to reserved headcount vs contractors.

Appendix: quick templates and checklists (paste-ready)
- Reviewer checklist: paste rubric, evidence, one improvement suggestion, recommend (hire/hold/reject).
- Offer packet starter lines: short role-context + two key first-week goals + buddy name + tech contacts.
- Onboarding pre-start checklist: SSO invite sent, laptop shipped (Y/N), repo access granted, first-week PR assigned.

Notes to self: keep the playbook lightweight, emphasize async evidence, and protect reviewer time by limiting required syncs. Pilot with 3 teams (serving-runtime, platform-engineering, solutions-eng) for first quarter.
